Prachur Sah: 
Thank you, Michelle, and a very warm welcome to everyone joining us today. I have Abhishek 
Maheshwari, our Chief Financial Officer; and Dheeraj Agarwal, our Head of Investor Relations, 
on the call. Today, I will take you through our operational and financial performance for the 
quarter ended September 30, 2026.  
We are happy to share that we recorded a strong growth in co-location additions in Q2. This has 
translated into an improvement in our tenancy ratio from 1.62 to 1.63, following a period of 
stability. Growth during the quarter was driven by continued network expansion from our 
customers, alongside a pickup in rollouts by a major customer.  
With healthy order book visibility and accelerating rollout activity, we expect the growth 
momentum to continue. Importantly, we continue to be the preferred infrastructure partner for 
our key customers, capturing a substantial share of their incremental rollouts. Our extensive 
footprint, superior network management capabilities, stringent SLA commitments and 
collaborative approach continue to reinforce customer trust and position us well to capture the 
next phase of industry growth. 
Our consistent performance and strong customer trust are underpinned by a deep sense of 
ownership of our frontline teams. During the quarter, our teams across Northeast, Bihar & 
Jharkhand and UP East, once again demonstrated exceptional resilience in the face of severe 
floods that disrupted network operations, restricted site access and caused prolonged power 
outages. Despite these challenges, our team responded with agility, proactive planning and close 
local coordination to accelerate restoration efforts and ensure service continuity across most of 
the affected networks. Their dedication in such challenging circumstances reflects the strength 
of our execution culture and our commitment to delivering reliable services to customers. 
The favorable regulatory environment has been supporting the seamless deployment of telecom 
infrastructure. Government support for smart meter deployment on telecom towers has further 
reinforced telecom infrastructure as a priority consumer category. Over the last three years, we 
have deployed smart meters on approximately 140,000 sites. This development provides 
improved visibility of consumption patterns and creates opportunities for energy optimization, 
operational efficiency and data-driven decision making.

Coming to the 5G networks. According to the recent TRAI data, India's 5G subscriber base grew 
by 36 million in the first quarter, exceeding 463 million subscribers. This secular demand curve 
is driving sustained operator investment in coverage and capacity. With the industry adding 
approximately 30,000 5G BTSs during the second quarter, taking the total installed base to 
around 593,000. As these networks mature, deployment focus is shifting towards network 
densification to support higher traffic loads and emerging digital use cases. Given our 
comprehensive portfolio and strength of customer relationships, we are structurally well 
positioned to support this steady infrastructure expansion. 
Infrastructure expansion and sustained 5G adoption trends are validated by robust consumption 
trends. In Q1, total data volume increased by 30% year-on-year, supported by an 18% rise in 
average monthly usage per subscriber. Notably, 5G networks are accelerating this trend, with 
5G usage alone growing 79% year-on-year, representing 44% of total data consumption, up from 
32% in the prior year. This ongoing shift highlights the necessity for sustained investments in 
network capacity, which supports long-term utilization rates and tenancy growth on our passive 
shared infrastructure. 
Our operational performance witnessed strong order bookings led by sustained customer rollouts 
and increased network expansion by a major customer. We added approximately 2,900 macro 
towers and robust co-locations of 7,900, marking year-on-year growth of 5.6% in towers and 
5.9% in co-locations. Our total macro tower and co-location base reached approximately 
270,500 and 440,200, respectively. Our industry-leading tenancy ratio has also improved from 
1.62 to 1.63, driven by substantial rollout through sharing of our existing towers. Including 
leaner sites, we concluded the quarter with approximately 454,200 co-locations, reinforcing our 
market-leading operational scale.  
We remain committed to supporting our customers' network expansion through our shared 
portfolio. We are actively collaborating with one of our major customers to facilitate its planned 
network rollouts, which is reflected in our consistent performance. Given our ready-to-deploy 
asset base, optimized geographical footprints and competitive value proposition, we remain 
confident in our ability to serve as a key long-term infrastructure partner for their network 
deployment plans. 
 
Our strategy of operating a low-cost shared infrastructure model provides the best solution to 
customers and Indus by way of improving asset productivity. With a large portfolio of towers 
designed to support multiple tenants, Indus remains the preferred partner for operators seeking 
rapid network expansion at an efficient cost. The company is equally well positioned to support 
existing customers in strategically important locations, where finding alternative infrastructure 
options may be difficult or less economical, particularly for a second and a third tenant. As a 
result, we remain confident to expand and retain co-locations at Indus from all the major 
customers. 
In addition, we remain committed to serving our customers with best-in-class service delivery 
and uptime, lower operating costs through tenancy profile and lower unit energy cost compared 
to other providers, which is critical for our customers' operations.

Indus continues to create bespoke solutions that provide customers with options to offer 
connectivity in public infrastructure such as airports, metros, tunnels, etcetera. During the 
quarter, Indus provided solutions for India Mobile Congress and enabled connectivity at Vizag 
Airport, and it is actively participating in similar projects. Supported by a specialized team 
focused on design and execution, the company has led incremental market share gains in new 
IBS deployments for two consecutive years and remains focused on expanding its presence in 
this segment while enhancing the end user connectivity experience. 
 
I would like to highlight that our determination to deliver superior service delivery resulted in 
sequential improvement in our network uptime from 99.955% to 99.97% despite challenging 
seasonal weather. Continuous technology deployments have enhanced our real-time network 
visibility, driving superior diagnostic and preventive capabilities that keep our customers 
seamlessly connected. 
 
Let me now provide an update on our energy management measures and the progress we have 
made. Our energy margin performance was driven by an 11% year-on-year reduction in diesel 
consumption. Our efforts for enabling digital energy management at our sites through remote 
connectivity, system-driven diesel planning, installation of fuel sensors and smart meters have 
started yielding positive results, while we believe there is still a long way to go. We optimized 
energy costs by deploying solar solutions across approximately 3,000 sites during Q2, increasing 
the solar site portfolio to 49,000 sites. Our planned transition from diesel to lithium-ion battery 
storage is progressing well and we are on track to meaningfully reduce dependence on diesel.  
Our ongoing digital transformation remains a key enabler for network reliability and operating 
efficiency. Deployment of AI-native digital solutions is enhancing field productivity and 
analytics. Implementation of AI-led image analytics is strengthening governance, vendor 
accountability and maintenance quality. Furthermore, office digitalization through a 
combination of automated energy billing, digital twin capabilities and real-time dashboards is 
streamlining decision-making and reducing manual effort. These strategic initiatives are 
successfully transitioning Indus Towers towards a predictive data-driven operating model, 
continuously improving organizational efficiency and customer experience. 
Our commitment to sustainable growth continues to drive meaningful ESG and value chain 
outcomes. In environmental stewardship, we accelerated our decarbonization journey, 
expanding our renewable energy footprint to an installed solar capacity of 297 megawatts in Q2 
from 259 megawatts in Q1. 
Safety remains a core priority. During the quarter, we launched Safety Shield Awards to 
recognize exemplary safety performance across our teams and partners, further strengthening 
our culture of safety and accountability. 
 
Through our flagship CSR initiatives, Saksham and Pragati, we positively impacted over 11 
million lives this quarter, while actively supporting communities affected by natural disasters 
and humanitarian challenges in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and UP.

Our ESG assessments and capability building initiatives continue to strengthen a more resilient 
value chain. During the quarter, ESG maturity assessments across 70 partners resulted in an 8% 
improvement in average ESG maturity scores. We are pleased to report that our CRISIL ESG 
rating improved from 57 to 63, complemented by recognition at Mahatma Awards and Business 
World Sustainable World Awards. Together, these milestones underscore our focus on creating 
long-term value through responsible and resilient operations. 
 
Coming to Africa. Our Africa foray is gaining strong traction, proving the competitiveness and 
the cost leadership of Indus' operating model. By achieving considerable capex savings per tower 
compared to competitors, we are delivering lower cost solutions for our anchor customer. 
Rollouts have successfully commenced with initial tower deployments as planned and are 
scheduled to ramp up in H2. We have also initiated engagements beyond our anchor customer 
to leverage our tenancy-led business model. Africa expansion is a long-term strategy, and we 
strongly believe we have a right to win. 
 
I would now request Abhishek to take you through our financial performance, and I look forward 
to your questions. Thank you, and over to you, Abhishek.

the quarter ended September 30, 2026. 
We witnessed a strong addition of co-locations during the quarter on the back of continued 
network expansion by our customers. The operational momentum has supported steady revenue 
growth and robust cash generation, reinforcing the strength of our infrastructure sharing model. 
 
Talking about financial performance for Q2. Revenue for the company grew at 1% quarter-on-
quarter and the revenue absolute value stands at INR85.2 billion. Core revenue for the rental is 
up by 1.3% quarter-on-quarter, stands at INR54.5 billion, driven by steady co-location addition 
and asset loading. This was further supported by acceleration of network rollout by major 
customers during the quarter. On year-on-year performance, our reported revenue and core 
revenue grew by 4% and 3.9%, respectively. 
 
Moving on to profitability. Reported EBITDA increased by 2.5% quarter-on-quarter and stands 
at INR46.3 billion for the quarter. Our EBITDA margin also improved by 80 basis points 
quarter-on-quarter and stands at 54.4% for the quarter. Please note that Q2 of last fiscal year 
included write-backs of approximately INR2 billion, relating to collection of overdue 
receivables from a major customer. Adjusting this one-off, our EBITDA grew at 5.2% year-on-
year. 
 
Our energy margin was negative 3.6% in Q2 compared to negative of 4.6% in Q1 and negative 
4.8% in the corresponding quarter of last year, reflecting a significant improvement during the 
reported quarter. Our structured energy efficiency measures are yielding positive results, and 
diesel consumption is further reduced by 11% year-on-year. Our continued focus on technology-
led energy management, including diesel optimization, enhanced visibility into electricity 
consumption and adoption of advanced battery solutions is lowering energy cost while 
strengthening our competitive position and energy performance.

Profit after tax was up by 2.7% quarter-on-quarter and stands at INR17.9 billion, driven by 
significant growth in EBITDA. Adjusting for the earlier mentioned write-back, PAT for the 
company grew at 6.4% year-on-year. 
Our capital productivity remains very efficient. From the trailing 12 months, we delivered a 
pretax return on capital employed of 25.3% and post-tax return on equity of 19.2%. The capital 
efficiency is reflected in our cash generation, with the free cash flow remaining robust at INR14 
billion for the quarter. The liquidity profile provides us with financial flexibility to support 
sustainable, value-accretive capital expenditure. 
 
Turning to Africa. We have successfully deployed towers in Zambia and Uganda in Q2 and also 
started generating revenue. In line with our phased rollout plan, we are set to begin deployment 
in Nigeria during the current quarter and our early capex performance per tower remains within 
the plan, validating our cost model during the initial phases. As the portfolio reaches to a more 
representative scale, we intend to share more detail on operational and financial metrics in 
subsequent quarters. By leveraging our disciplined and cost-efficient shared infrastructure model 
and robust network management, we are confident in our ability to become credible player and 
actively support Africa long-term digital infrastructure demand. 
 
To conclude, our Q2 performance underscored the resilience of our business model, underpinned 
by healthy order book and sustained customer rollout. Looking ahead, our focus on operating 
efficiency, structure energy cost optimization and technology integration will continue to 
support profitability. Further, our expansion into Africa progresses on schedule, representing a 
measured extension of our core competencies. We remain committed to executing profitable 
growth opportunities and driving sustainable long-term value for shareholders. 
 
With that, now I hand it back to Michelle to open the floor for questions.
